verification_report.summary: Both proofs are correct under the explicitly accepted internal premises, conditional only on item 5: cor:big-relative-supersolution for every nonzero finite NPP measure under the same BMP, arbitrary smooth big real background, and positive-lower-model-volume hypotheses. The sequential audit verifies every exponential-order direction and establishes genuine L1 limits before invoking fixed-dominator continuity. The weighted-mass supremum is attained: bounded-exponential convergence in L1 of the fixed measure and continuous L1 approximation identify MA(w)=exp(w)nu; non-pluripolarity justifies removing the weight across pole sets. The residual supersolution meets the addition theorem's bounded-carrier hypothesis and forces saturation. Nonzero carrier truncations, their decreasing solutions, dominated convergence, simultaneous scaling, and positive-exponent uniqueness all pass. For zero exponent, the coefficients stay uniformly positive, normalization yields a genuine limit in E_phi, and exp(v_j/j) has a common lower curvature bound and converges to one in L1(mu). The retained exponents are exactly 1/j_k, giving total-variation convergence to c mu. Integration gives ell/mu(X)<=c<=M/mu(X); strict domination proves uniqueness of c without asserting normalized-potential uniqueness. The attribution to [XL26, Theorems 6.1–6.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.13446v1) is verified. Its conclusions and standing global positive-volume assumption are not imported. No semipositivity or closedness of theta, no independent global PVP, and no ordinary-type conclusion u approximately phi are used. No critical errors or gaps were found.
